researchUpdates.title: Performance-driven mix design and multi-response optimization of ambient-cured fly ash-GGBFS based geopolymer concrete
researchUpdates.authors: Md Ruhul Amin, Mohd Shariq, Abdul Baqi and Mohd Asif Ansari
researchUpdates.summary: An 18-mixture factorial experiment evaluates ambient-cured fly-ash/slag geopolymer concrete across slag replacement, alkaline-liquid-to-binder ratio and two predefined mixture levels, then applies response-surface optimization to fresh and mechanical responses.
highlights: The experiment measures slump plus 7- and 28-day compressive and splitting-tensile strengths, allowing the workability and strength objectives to be optimized together within the tested factor ranges.

The selected optima occur at the upper tested slag level, so the fitted response surfaces support interpolation within this design space rather than proving that still-higher slag fractions would continue the same trend.
researchUpdates.access: Single laboratory program, not independent replication. The optimized settings depend on the tested materials, fixed activator conditions and chosen constraints. Modulus of rupture was estimated from a prior relationship rather than directly measured here and must not be treated as a flexural test result.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary publisher metadata, full article text and author information; no figures, tables, supplementary files or data were reproduced

journalArticle.title: An optimum needs edges
journalArticle.summary: A useful optimization result records not only its selected mixture, but also the tested bounds and which responses were actually measured.
paragraphs: The new study combines workability, compressive strength and splitting-tensile strength in a constrained response-surface search. That is more informative than optimizing one outcome alone, but the result remains tied to eighteen mixtures, two predefined design levels and fixed activator choices.

For the formulation database, every optimized recipe should retain its factor ranges, constraints, curing regime and response type. A boundary optimum is not evidence that moving beyond the boundary will improve performance, and an estimated modulus of rupture is not a measured flexural-strength result.
